overview: This 1936–1939 file documents U.S. review of Japanese fisheries and training vessels’ requests to visit Alaska, the Aleutians, the Philippines, and Hawaii. Diplomatic notes and interdepartmental correspondence weigh fur seal research, port restrictions, naval concerns, and customary courtesies. Decisions range from denied harbor access to narrowly permitted emergency calls and approved visits.
interest: Reversals and conditional permissions reveal how seal research, naval concerns, and fisheries diplomacy shaped access to restricted harbors.
